prompt: Write 5 short claim log entries by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim. Injury: wrist fracture. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1232; do not mention it.)
text:
Entry 1: Claim opened following a report of a collision at an intersection. Insured vehicle was turning left when it was struck by an oncoming vehicle proceeding straight. Initial contact made with the claimant, who reports a wrist injury and is handling the matter without legal representation. Photos of both vehicles requested.

Entry 2: Received photos of the damage to the insured vehicle, showing front driver-side impact. Claimant's vehicle photos show rear quarter panel damage. Scene diagram obtained from the claimant. Both parties agree the light was green for the oncoming vehicle at the time of impact. Liability appears to lean toward the insured based on the left-turn sequence, pending review of statements.

Entry 3: Claimant reports a fractured wrist diagnosed at urgent care, with a splint applied and a follow-up with an orthopedic specialist scheduled. Requested copies of the medical records and the treatment plan. Claimant confirmed no attorney has been retained and asked about the claims process. Explained the general steps and the documents needed to proceed.

Entry 4: Statement taken from the insured, who says they began the turn when the signal turned yellow and did not see the oncoming vehicle until impact. Witness contact information obtained from the insured's passenger for follow-up. Police report requested and has not yet been received. Reserve set pending medical documentation.

Entry 5: Follow-up call with the claimant to confirm receipt of the medical request forms. Claimant is still in a splint and has been missing work, and asked about rental coverage for transportation. Advised the claimant to keep all receipts for related expenses. Liability review continues. Next step is to obtain the police report and the orthopedic records before making any determination on settlement.
